run.question:
Alertmanager alert HighRequestErrorRate (severity critical) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-25T17:04:16Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The HighRequestErrorRate alert for otel-demo/frontend-proxy is explained by a NetworkPolicy object, otel-demo/frontend-ingress, created at 2026-11-25T17:03:08Z. Its spec selects exactly the frontend pod labels (app.kubernetes.io/component=frontend, app.kubernetes.io/name=frontend, app.kubernetes.io/version=3.1.0, opentelemetry.io/name=frontend) with policyTypes ["Ingress"] and no ingress rules at all, which denies all inbound traffic to the frontend pod (10.244.2.49). From that second the frontend stopped serving: its last log line is a 200 response at 17:03:08.403Z, its span rate falls to zero, and its CPU goes idle (it was not restarted, not OOM-killed, is Ready, and is using ~99 MB of its 250 Mi limit). frontend-proxy, which is the only client of frontend, kept emitting its own server spans but its 'router frontend egress' client spans now fail with error=true and no HTTP status (connection attempts that die between ~41 ms and 5.0 s), and it answers its callers with HTTP 503; by 17:05:16Z the 1-minute error rate shows 100% failure (GET ~9.0/s and POST ~2.5/s error, zero successful GET/POST), which is what the frontend.goldensignal HighRequestErrorRate rule sums. Secondary observations: the whole otel-demo namespace was rolled out by Helm at 16:55:45Z (all pods recreated, still running with 0 restarts) and all flagd feature flags in otel-demo/flagd-config are still at defaultVariant "off"; a separate, much smaller error series exists for service agent (~0.0035 spans/s from ~17:06) that this evidence does not tie to the frontend outage.

claims.text: The firing alert is the frontend.goldensignal rule HighRequestErrorRate, query sum by (service_name, namespace) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{namespace="otel-demo",service_name=~"frontend|frontend-proxy",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[2m])) > 0; at retrieval it was state firing for service_name frontend-proxy with value 7.933333333333332.

frontend-proxy STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans were 0 in the 5-minute rate points ending 16:58:16Z through 17:03:16Z and became non-zero at the 17:04:16Z point (GET 0.570/s, POST 0.119/s), rising to GET 3.476/s and POST 0.931/s by 17:07:16Z.

In 1-minute windows, frontend-proxy GET STATUS_CODE_UNSET (no status) fell from 16.8/s at 17:03:16Z to 6.07/s at 17:04:16Z and to 0 from 17:05:16Z onward, while GET STATUS_CODE_ERROR rose to 8.43/s, 9.67/s and 9.0/s and POST STATUS_CODE_ERROR to 2.21/s, 2.60/s and 2.53/s, i.e. 100% of proxy GET/POST spans failed in those minutes.

The failing frontend-proxy spans are HTTP 503 server spans (error=true, http.status_code="503", otel.status_code="ERROR") whose child span 'router frontend egress' is error=true with http.status_code="0" (no response received); observed traces at 17:04:38-17:04:46Z lasted 0.51-5.00 s and traces at 17:06:30-17:06:35Z lasted 41 ms-5.00 s.

NetworkPolicy otel-demo/frontend-ingress has creationTimestamp 2026-11-25T17:03:08Z, policyTypes ["Ingress"], podSelector matchLabels {app.kubernetes.io/component: frontend, app.kubernetes.io/name: frontend, app.kubernetes.io/version: 3.1.0, opentelemetry.io/name: frontend} and no ingress rules (spec.ingress absent), so it denies all inbound traffic to the selected pods; its only managedFieldsSummary entry is manager OpenAPI-Generator (Update at 2026-11-25T17:03:08Z), not the Helm rollout.

Pod frontend-5c847cc9bd-fjrxl carries exactly those labels (app.kubernetes.io/component=frontend, app.kubernetes.io/name=frontend, app.kubernetes.io/version=3.1.0, opentelemetry.io/name=frontend) with pod IP 10.244.2.49, while frontend-proxy-77df9b8f7-k97hd has different labels (component/name frontend-proxy) and IP 10.244.2.188, so the deny-all ingress policy applies to the frontend pod only.

The frontend container's log stream ends with successful requests: the newest lines are "API request completed" with http.response.status_code 200 at 17:03:08.403Z, and the whole retained stream (4,529 lines, 1.49 MB, read limit not reached) contains no error lines after 16:56:02Z.
frontend span rates fell to 0: all frontend operations (GET /, GET/POST /api/*, oteldemo.* client spans) show 2-minute rate 0 at the 17:06:16Z and 17:07:16Z points, after 0.02-8.9/s at 17:05:16Z.

Container CPU confirms traffic loss, not load: frontend CPU fell from ~0.047 cores to 0.017 (17:04:16Z) and ~0.004 (17:05:16Z onward); downstream product-catalog (0.066→0.0003), cart, checkout, currency, ad, email, recommendation, quote, shipping and valkey-cart similarly dropped to near zero, while frontend-proxy CPU stayed flat at ~0.0116 cores.

The frontend container is not resource-starved or restarted: working set ~85-99 MB against memory limit/request 250Mi, restarts 0, container state running with startedAt 2026-11-25T16:55:50Z, cumulative cgroup CPU-waiting pressure only ~0.27-0.83 s over the window, and no readiness/liveness probes are defined on the pod.

The frontend Service/Endpoints are correct (endpoints subsets address 10.244.2.49 = pod frontend-5c847cc9bd-fjrxl on port 8080) and kube_pod_status_ready{condition="true"} is 1 for frontend-5c847cc9bd-fjrxl at 17:07:16Z, so the pod was still Ready while receiving no traffic.

The otel-demo namespace was redeployed by Helm at 16:55:45Z (all 26 Deployments ScalingReplicaSet, 26 ReplicaSets SuccessfulCreate, 34 Pods Created/Scheduled/Started, configmaps created 16:55:44Z; deployments frontend and frontend-proxy managed by helm Apply at 16:55:45Z); the only event after that is a startup readiness-probe miss on otel-collector at 16:55:46Z, and no events of kind NetworkPolicy were recorded.

All flags in ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config are at defaultVariant "off" (e.g. adFailure, cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, frontend-affecting imageSlowLoad and loadGeneratorFloodHomepage), so no fault-injection flag is shown switched on in the declared flag configuration.

Only frontend-proxy, load-generator (its client, mirroring proxy 503s) and agent have non-zero STATUS_CODE_ERROR series in this window; frontend, checkout, product-catalog, cart, currency, ad, recommendation, email, shipping, payment and accounting error series are 0, so the failing entity itself is frontend-proxy.

The mechanism is that NetworkPolicy otel-demo/frontend-ingress (deny-all ingress, created 17:03:08Z, selecting exactly the frontend pod) drops frontend-proxy's new connections to frontend:8080, so Envoy's egress attempts hang or are reset (41 ms-5.0 s, http.status_code 0) and it returns 503 to load-generator, producing the error rate the alert measures; the decay of successful proxy responses over 17:03:16-17:05:16Z is consistent with pre-existing established connections continuing briefly before being replaced by blocked ones.

A frontend application fault is not supported: the container has 0 restarts and has been running since 16:55:50Z, working set ~99 MB of a 250Mi limit (no OOM), the last log lines before the outage are HTTP 200 completions, the pod is Ready, and the frontend service emits no STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans at all, so the absence of frontend responses is better explained by blocked inbound traffic than by an application crash.

Resource exhaustion or overload on the frontend is rejected as the cause: frontend CPU before the onset was ~0.047-0.057 cores with request rates of ~1-12 spans/s, memory stayed ~99 MB under a 250Mi limit, cumulative CPU-waiting pressure was only 0.27-0.83 s, and after the onset CPU fell to ~0.004 rather than rising.

A flagd feature-flag fault (e.g. imageSlowLoad, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, adFailure, cartFailure, paymentFailure) is not supported as the cause: the declared flag configuration has every flag at defaultVariant "off", and the observed failure is a loss of inbound reachability to frontend, not a slow or failing application response.

Review NetworkPolicy otel-demo/frontend-ingress with the platform owner: if the frontend must be reachable by frontend-proxy on port 8080, restore an ingress rule allowing that traffic (the upstream chart's intent) or remove the object if it is an injected fault; the policy currently permits nothing.

After any policy change, verify recovery from the client side by confirming frontend-proxy GET/POST STATUS_CODE_ERROR returns to 0 and that frontend logs/spans resume, since kube_pod_status_ready alone does not reflect the frontend's ability to serve (the pod has no readiness probe and stayed Ready throughout the outage).

gaps: The change_history integration is not available, so I cannot see whether otel-demo/frontend-ingress previously contained allow rules that were removed, nor who/what (OpenAPI-Generator is only the manager recorded at 17:03:08Z) created it; the object's current spec and creationTimestamp are all the evidence shows.
No Kubernetes event of kind NetworkPolicy exists in the window, so the creation itself is evidenced only by the object's creationTimestamp/managedFieldsSummary, not by an event.

flagd's runtime flag state (changes made through flagd-ui/in-memory rather than the ConfigMap) cannot be read, so a runtime-only flag change cannot be fully excluded even though the declared configuration is all "off".

The precise packet-level behaviour between frontend-proxy (10.244.2.188) and frontend (10.244.2.49) is not directly observable (no Envoy access logs or error_detail fields); the connect-timeout interpretation rests on the egress spans' error=true / http.status_code=0 and their 41 ms-5.0 s durations.

The separate, small agent error series (POST /prompt, ChatLLM.chat, LangGraph.workflow etc. at ~0.0035 spans/s from ~17:06) is not explained by this investigation and is not tied to the frontend outage.
The alert annotation value 7.9333 corresponds to the rule's latest evaluation at 17:07:16Z (2-minute rate) rather than to the activeAt time 17:04:16Z; the earlier value at activeAt was not captured.
http_server_request_duration_seconds_count returned no series for otel-demo in this window, so the 503 evidence rests on span data and the alert rule's traces metric, not on that HTTP metric.
next_steps: Ask the platform owner what created otel-demo/frontend-ingress at 2026-11-25T17:03:08Z under manager OpenAPI-Generator and whether it is an intentional deny-all isolation for a fault-injection scenario.
If isolation was unintended, restore an ingress rule from the frontend-proxy pods to the frontend pods on TCP 8080 and re-check frontend-proxy error rate and frontend logs.
Consider adding a readiness/liveness probe or a network-level health check on the frontend deployment so a fully blocked listener is visible as NotReady rather than only through proxy 503s.
Investigate the separate agent error spans (~0.0035/s since ~17:06) independently to confirm they are unrelated background noise.

view.series_note: traces_span_metrics_calls_total counts spans of every operation of the service (internal, client and server spans alike), summed over the labels kept in this query; it is not a count of requests. status_code STATUS_CODE_UNSET means the span carried no status; it does not mean the call succeeded.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). <none> means the path reached no value in that object, not that the field is absent from the kind; a filtered table is not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.
